clue.text: Appreciation of taste shown by friend having had food

parts.note: a pal is a friend
ate means had food, past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A gourmet's discernment is on show when a companion has dined.
explanation.definitionFit: A discerning palate is a person's sense and judgement of flavour.

clue.text: Bower providing shelter for cockney

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the H at the start of words, so the initial H goes

parts.note: a harbour is a shelter, as a verb or a noun

explanation.surface: A leafy garden retreat offers a Londoner somewhere to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, known for dropping initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shady garden recess, the same as a leafy arbour.

clue.text: Unusually, girls let teacher do what a teacher must do

definitions.text: do what a teacher must do

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an odd way, so the letters of the next three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some girls are oddly allowed to stand in for the teacher at a vital task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges GIRLS LET TEACHER into the phrase; British teachers take attendance this way each morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking attendance by reading out pupils' names is a routine classroom duty.

clue.text: Hide in the home counties, then somewhere in the Med

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England, SE
Crete is an island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A fugitive lies low near London, then flees to a Mediterranean hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it somewhere out of sight.

clue.text: Act as cabby bound for pub and be extremely annoying

parts.note: a cabby's job is to drive a passenger, to drive one
heading to the pub is going to drink

explanation.surface: A taxi driver heading to the pub is a terrible nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: A cabby is a taxi driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone so exasperating they push others towards alcohol.

clue.text: Judy's heart, full of adoration, becoming elevated

indicators.note: full of means the outer letters hold the next piece within
the heart of a word is its central part, here the two middle letters of the name

parts.note: praise is adoration or worship

explanation.surface: Judy is besotted, her heart full of love and her spirits lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judy's heart' points at the girl's name, but only its two central letters are used, wrapped round the word for adoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upraised is lifted up, held high.

clue.text: Contents of a cold urn poured out into kettle

indicators.note: poured out suggests the letters spilling and resettling in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tips the cold contents of an urn into a kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' joins the surface; 'poured out' rearranges A COLD URN.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettle is an old word for a large metal cooking pot, as in a kettle of fish.

clue.text: Male-female relationship hurt by one in temper

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for temper

parts.note: rage is a fit of temper
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A relationship is spoiled when one partner loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like a verb next to 'hurt', but it is the noun for an angry fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding union is traditionally the bond between husband and wife.

clue.text: Material put down for another recording

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
to lay is to put down

explanation.surface: Fabric is laid down to make a fresh recording, perhaps for soundproofing.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat broadcast or second playing of a match or tape is a rerun.

clue.text: Foreign character seen in hitchin

indicators.note: seen in means the letters sit inside the town name

explanation.surface: An unusual person from abroad is spotted in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchin is a market town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the Greek alphabet is a foreign written symbol.

clue.text: Wait about by a posh car

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: Someone loiters beside a luxury vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait' is not a verb: waits were Christmas street singers. A Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: Waits were bands of carol singers going from house to house at Christmas.

clue.text: Entering base, sailor likely to work

indicators.note: entering means the seaman goes inside the word for base

parts.note: base means vile or low
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor going into a naval base has every chance of finding a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A viable plan is a feasible one that can succeed.

clue.text: Take the dominant position? A Scotsman often doesn't!

explanation.surface: Pondering who is boss, with a quip about kilts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be the one in charge at home; literally, Scots in kilts are not putting on breeches.

clue.text: One even higher than the king

explanation.surface: A single card outranks the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In dice and cards the top card counts as one, and in many games it ranks above the king.

clue.text: Train cut restricting salesperson

indicators.note: restricting means the word for cut holds the salesperson inside it

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut
a rep, sales representative, is a salesperson

explanation.surface: A rail service is reduced, leaving a travelling salesman stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to get ready or make fit for a task.

clue.text: Dealer is exceptionally accomplished

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at things done out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card dealer is unusually skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Realised means achieved or brought about, as an ambition is fulfilled.

clue.text: Awful riot with play engendering opposition

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful riot during a play provokes hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Polarity is the state of having two opposite poles or contrary tendencies.

clue.text: Money being short stopping repair

parts.note: money in short form is the abbreviation M
an ending is a stopping or finish

explanation.surface: Cash running low halts the repair work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mending is the work of fixing something broken or torn.

clue.text: Enthusiasm when female departs or anger?

indicators.note: departs means the woman's letter leaves the word for enthusiasm

parts.note: fire means passion or enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Does passion turn to rage when a woman walks out?
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath.

clue.text: Distant saint going over the mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue the saint sits above, over, the mountains

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A remote holy man crosses a mountain chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange can mean aloof or unfamiliar in manner, cool and remote.

clue.text: Blatant overcharging, but hardly a "dark deed"?

explanation.surface: Daring overpricing is no secret crime done at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a flagrant rip-off; literally, a theft in broad day is no dark deed.

clue.text: Pad worn by woman once creating commotion

explanation.surface: A woman's undergarment causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian frame or pad padded out the back of a skirt; it also means busy activity.

clue.text: Having French wine wrapped in cloth is mad

indicators.note: wrapped in means the wine sits inside the cloth

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Wrapping a bottle of French wine in a cloth is crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Raving means wildly irrational, as in raving lunatic.

clue.text: With energy draining away from the cat that is on the river

indicators.note: draining away from means energy leaves the word for the big cat

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy ebbs from a big cat by a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draining away from' takes E out of TIGER to leave TIGR.
explanation.definitionFit: This Middle Eastern waterway flows through Turkey and Iraq.

clue.text: A rev. Is put out by a bishop being harsh

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reverend is displaced by a bishop in a severe move.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasive manner is rough and grating.

clue.text: Cask silly person knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means tipped upside down, so in an across clue the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a crazy or silly person

explanation.surface: A barrel tipped over a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large barrel for wine or beer.

clue.text: Resort made 'er ecstatic, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the letters are spelt the way the phrase sounds

parts.note: to send someone is to thrill them, so sent 'er

explanation.surface: A holiday spot thrilled her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' is slang for thrilled; 'er drops the H as in casual speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre can be a place people go for an activity, like a holiday or leisure venue.

clue.text: Tall, ungainly heather follows the crowd

indicators.note: follows means the plant comes after the crowd

parts.note: a gang is a crowd or group
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: A lanky youth trails after the crowd across the heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone lanky and awkward.
